newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's CIR makes OPA for Sasib shares.
newsitem.headline: Italy's CIR makes OPA for Sasib shares.

text.p: CIR, the industrial holding company of Italian financier Carlo De Benedetti, said on Saturday it intended to make a public buy offer (OPA) for shares in engineering company Sasib.
CIR said in a statement it would start proceedings for an OPA on all ordinary and savings shares in Sasib Spa held by minority shareholders.
The OPA would also extend to all bonds in circulation which had been issued by Sasib International BV convertible into Sasib savings shares.
CIR said it currently holds 54.4 percent of Sasib Spa's ordinary shares.
CIR estimated the total operation at 475.1 billion lire.

It said it intended to offer 5,800 lire per ordinary share, 3,400 lire per savings share and 3,400 lire for each Sasib International BV bond expiring December 31, 1997 and convertible into Sasib savings shares at a rate of one for one.

CIR said the offer prices represented an increase of 26.8 percent on ordinary shares and 18.4 percent on savings shares compared with average prices for the stock registered on the bourse in the course of this month.
Both CIR and Sasib shares were suspended on the Milan bourse on Friday pending the announcement. CIR ordinary shares ended on Thursday at 1033 lire and Sasib ordinary shares closed at 4900.
CIR said it had been advised by Italian merchant bank Mediobanca for the operation and subject to approval by stock market watchdog Consob, the OPA would get underway at the start of June.
The holding company said it was carrying out the move in order to reinforce its presence in the engineering sector.
The OPA was also part of a wider project currently underway to rationalise CIR's industrial activities.
